questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The history, burials and legends of St. Patrick's Church
Catholic landownership laws in colonial Nova Scotia
A stone-masonry guide to Cape Breton's historic churches
How to plan a seasonal visit around Cape Breton Island
questions.explain: It covers the church's origins, burials and reported paranormal tales.

questions.q: Why did Captain Wilson buy land in Sydney?
options: To build a market house for the Sydney Garrison
To bury his infant son in a Catholic ceremony
To build a small fort for the garrison's soldiers
To build a school for the local Catholic children
questions.explain: Sydney had no Catholic cemetery for the couple's infant son.

questions.q: What did workers uncover during the Old Sydney Society's restoration work?
options: A set of old burial records and maps
The red bell from the Market House
Human remains beneath the floorboards
An intact wooden chapel structure
questions.explain: Workers found the remains of Captain Wilson and seven other individuals under the floorboards.

questions.q: What happens if you ring the red bell three times, per legend?
options: Footsteps are heard on the balcony
The upstairs door to the belfry opens
The church lights flicker on and off
A ghost appears at the belfry window
questions.explain: The legend says the upstairs door leading to the belfry opens on its own.

questions.q: Why were all reburied but Wilson given Catholic rites?
options: Wilson had been Anglican
Wilson was unidentified
His wife objected
Wilson refused
questions.explain: Catholic rites were performed for all except Wilson, who was Anglican.
